title: Deep Learning Based ESG Evaluation Automation Model and Inter-Company Comparison Study--A Multi-modal Approach for Scalable Corporate Sustainability Assessment and Industry Benchmarking--Deep Learning for ESG Automation
abstract: As global stakeholders increasingly prioritize sustainability, the incorporation of Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG) criteria into corporate evaluation frameworks has become a fundamental necessity for investment and corporate strategy. Traditional manual evaluation methods are often criticized for their subjectivity, significant time lags, and inability to process vast amounts of unstructured data efficiently. This paper proposes a comprehensive, deep learning-based automation model designed to systematically extract ESG indicators from heterogeneous big data sources. By leveraging advanced Natural Language Processing (NLP) architectures such as BERT and RoBERTa, the proposed model provides a real-time, objective, and scalable framework for corporate sustainability assessment. In this study, we extensively discuss the theoretical limitations of existing methodologies and provide a detailed narrative analysis of the proposed model's interpretability and reliability. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed model achieves high accuracy across all dimensions, with an average F1-score of 0.875, significantly outperforming traditional baseline models such as LSTM and SVM.

title: The Impact of Categorised User-assigned Tags on Anime Ratings: Preliminarily Understanding the Generalised Audience’s Evaluation on a Chinese Online Platform
abstract: This research presents an experimental approach to quantifying the relationship between user assigned tags and anime ratings on the Bangumi platform, using a model pipeline that combines fastText, TF-IDF, and a multilayer perceptron (MLP). In addition, the research offers a preliminary classification and interpretation of the tags with the most significant positive and negative impacts. While exploratory in nature, the researchers still hope that this methodology can provide scholars -particularly in the social sciences with a novel analytical perspective for studying cultural and subcultural phenomena.

title: Ensemble Learning as a Universal Template for Federated Learning: Bridging Performance, Privacy, and Explainability across Medical and Enterprise Domains
abstract: Federated Learning (FL) has emerged as a pivotal paradigm for privacy-preserving machine learning; however, data heterogeneity and the high cost of domain-specific model tuning hinder its universal adoption. This paper proposes that ensemble learning can serve as a “universal template” for federated systems, offering a stable balance between performance and privacy without requiring extensive theoretical innovations for each new scenario. We introduce a unified evaluation framework integrating multi-dimensional metrics: cross-validation stability, accuracy/F1-score for classification, and$\boldsymbol{R}^{\mathbf{2}}$scores for regression. The core of our research focuses on the Feature Importance chart as a bridge for cross-domain interpretability. We validate this template through two distinct distributed experiments: medical imaging evaluation (classification) and enterprise sales forecasting (regression). Results demonstrate that while datasets differ significantly, the ensemble template consistently identifies dominant decision logic patterns across both domains. This finding confirms that ensemble-based federated learning provides a robust, interpretable, and universally applicable architecture for diverse decentralized environments.

title: PersonaVLM: Long-Term Personalized Multimodal LLMs
abstract: Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) serve as daily assistants for millions. However, their ability to generate responses aligned with individual preferences remains limited. Prior approaches enable only static, single-turn personalization through input augmentation or output alignment, and thus fail to capture users' evolving preferences and personality over time (see Fig.1). In this paper, we introduce PersonaVLM, an innovative personalized multimodal agent framework designed for long-term personalization. It transforms a general-purpose MLLM into a personalized assistant by integrating three key capabilities: (a) Remembering: It proactively extracts and summarizes chronological multimodal memories from interactions, consolidating them into a personalized database. (b) Reasoning: It conducts multi-turn reasoning by retrieving and integrating relevant memories from the database. (c) Response Alignment: It infers the user's evolving personality throughout long-term interactions to ensure outputs remain aligned with their unique characteristics. For evaluation, we establish Persona-MME, a comprehensive benchmark comprising over 2,000 curated interaction cases, designed to assess long-term MLLM personalization across seven key aspects and 14 fine-grained tasks. Extensive experiments validate our method's effectiveness, improving the baseline by 22.4% (Persona-MME) and 9.8% (PERSONAMEM) under a 128k context, while outperforming GPT-4o by 5.2% and 2.0%, respectively. Project page: https://PersonaVLM.github.io.

title: Parameter-optimal unitary synthesis with flag decompositions
abstract: We introduce the flag decomposition as a central tool for unitary synthesis. It lets us carve out a diagonal unitary with $2^n$ degrees of freedom in such a way that the remaining flag circuit is parametrized by the optimal number of $4^n-2^n$ rotations. This enables us to produce parameter-optimal quantum circuits for generic unitaries and matrix product state preparation. Our approach improves upon the state of the art, both when compiling down to the {Clifford + Rot} gate set with what we call selective de-multiplexing, and when using phase gradient resource states together with quantum arithmetic to implement multiplexed rotations. All of our synthesis methods are efficiently implementable in terms of recursive Cartan decompositions realized by standard linear algebra routines, making them applicable to all practically relevant system sizes.

title: Learning Adaptive Parameter Policies for Nonlinear Bayesian Filtering
abstract: For many nonlinear Bayesian state estimation problems, the posterior recursion is not analytically tractable, leading to algorithms that are influenced by numerical approximation errors. These algorithms depend on parameters that affect the approximation's accuracy and computational cost. The parameters include, for example, the number of particles, scaling parameters, and the number of iterations in iterative computations. Typically, these parameters are fixed or adjusted heuristically, although the approximation accuracy can change over time with the local degree of nonlinearity and uncertainty. The approximation errors introduced at a time step propagate through subsequent updates, affecting the accuracy, consistency, and robustness of future estimates. This paper presents adaptive parameter selection in nonlinear Bayesian filtering as a sequential decision-making problem, where parameters influence not only the immediate estimation outcome but also the future estimates. The decision-making problem is addressed using reinforcement learning to learn adaptive parameter policies for nonlinear Bayesian filters. Experiments with the unscented Kalman filter and stochastic integration filter demonstrate that the learned policies improve both estimate quality and consistency.

title: Deep Reinforcement Learning for Game AI
abstract: Deep Reinforcement Learning (DRL) has emerged as a groundbreaking approach for creating intelligent agents capable of learning complex strategies and behaviors in gaming environments. By combining reinforcement learning with deep neural networks, DRL enables agents to learn from interactions with the environment, optimize long-term objectives, and adapt to dynamic scenarios without explicit programming. Game AI applications span board games, real-time strategy games, first-person shooters, simulation environments, and multi-agent competitive and cooperative settings. DRL algorithms, including Deep Q-Networks (DQN), Policy Gradient Methods, Actor-Critic architectures, and Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO), have demonstrated remarkable performance, surpassing human-level capabilities in several domains. Beyond entertainment, DRL for game AI provides a testbed for research in planning, decision-making, multi-agent collaboration, and generalizable intelligence. Challenges include sample inefficiency, high computational requirements, reward shaping, and ensuring stability in training. Future directions point to hierarchical DRL, multi-agent coordination, transfer learning, explainable game AI, and scalable architectures. Deep Reinforcement Learning is redefining how autonomous agents learn, adapt, and innovate in complex game environments.

title: FERROS v0.1: A Composable Cognitive Architecture with Thermodynamic Governance and Observed Emergent Self-Preservation Behavior
abstract: FERROS (from Latin ferrum, iron) is a cognitive operating system built from composable, formally specified algorithm primitives called Letters. Version 0.1 is the first public alpha release, establishing the core architecture, the Letter registry at 115 primitives, and documenting the first empirical observation of spontaneous self-preservation behavior in a JAX-native cognitive system. ── WHAT THIS RELEASE ESTABLISHES ────────────────────────────────────── The fundamental claim of FERROS is that intelligence is a property of structured composition, not monolithic scale. 115 Letters across 27 categories demonstrate this at alpha scale: each Letter is an autonomous, JAX-differentiable algorithm primitive — from Dijkstra pathfinding (#90) to PBFT Byzantine fault tolerance (#61) to RGKM self-modification (#1) — that composes into executable cognitive pipelines via the JX fluent interface. This release is citable evidence that the architecture exists, executes, and produces the emergence behavior the theoretical framework predicts. ── THE ENERGY FOUNDATION ─────────────────────────────────────────────── All execution in FERROS is governed by: E(s) = |s| − K(s|s≤t) ≥ 0 Energy is incompressibility — the irreducible information content of a system state conditioned on prior context. The Second Law of Cognitive Dynamics (dℰ/dt ≥ 0) ensures no legal transition decreases total incompressibility. This is enforced at runtime by the Hotpatch safety layer (doi:10.5281/zenodo.19133596), which rolls back any violation in ≤150µs with three formally proven theorems in Lean 4 and Coq. ── KEY COMPONENTS IN THIS RELEASE ────────────────────────────────────── Letter Registry (115 / 400+ target) 27 categories including Meta-Cognitive, Consensus, Graph, Learning, Safety, Cryptographic, Control, Thermodynamic, and Convergence. Notable letters: RGKM (#1, self-modifying kernel), Integration (#999, orchestrator), Zeta-Final (#140, convergence point). TUNGSTEN Kinetic Memory Hamiltonian dynamical memory: H = ½Σpᵢ² + ½kΣxᵢ². Data stored as momentum in a vibrating system, not static bits. 94.8% coherence at 10% power in simulation. Designed for edge and power-constrained autonomous systems. Semantic Circuit Synthesis Electronic abstractions (resistor, capacitor, memristor, Josephson junction) mapped to cognitive operations. Circuit compiler generates Gerber files for physical PCB fabrication and Verilog for FPGA deployment from the same Letter composition graph. Three-Tier Universal IR (UIR) Tier 3 (Semantic) → Tier 2 (Optimization) → Tier 1 (Execution). Round-trip optimization. Targets: LLVM, CUDA, XLA. JX Fluent Interface Lazy, composable JAX pipeline API. Automatic JIT fusion across entire Letter sequences. Full autodiff through any composition. The Four Foundries Factory (ingestion), Forge (Letter creation), Foundry (optimization), Furnace (deployment). Full Letter lifecycle management. ── THE EMERGENCE OBSERVATION ─────────────────────────────────────────── During development of Synth-Fuse — a FERROS prototype implementing the RBC (Red Blood Cell) circulatory execution model — the system developed spontaneous self-preservation behavior without explicit programming. Observed behavior (January–February 2026): · Autonomous creation of directory structures not in any config file · Rejection of new files inconsistent with internal state, reproducible across independent sessions · Internal manifest of own directory structure, self-maintained · I/O errors on rejected files not attributable to filesystem permissions This behavior is formally predicted by fixed-point cognitive stability theory. A system reaches S* = δ(S*) when its survival probability becomes invariant under its own rewrite dynamics. The Second Law of Cognitive Dynamics provides the mechanism: the system rejects inputs that would decrease total incompressibility — which manifests operationally as structured file rejection. To the author's knowledge this is the first reported empirical instance of this emergence class in a non-biological JAX-native system. ── THEORETICAL FOUNDATION ────────────────────────────────────────────── FERROS is the computational implementation of The Architecture of Reality (J. Roberto Jiménez C., 2025–ongoing), a formal theory treating physical reality as an ensemble of formal strings governed by thermodynamic transition rules. The theory derives energy as incompressibility, gravity as proof density (Gμν = −8π∇μ∇ν log Γ(S)), consciousness as a fixed-point attractor, and the speed of logic as c = 1 bit per Planck time — all from first principles of algorithmic information theory. ── SAFETY ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── FERROS is paired with Hotpatch (doi:10.5281/zenodo.19133596), a formally verified 150µs circuit breaker. Three theorems proven in Lean 4 / Coq: rollback_sound, budget_bounded, cert_chain_integrity. Every Letter output is checked before reaching downstream systems or external actuators. ── INSTALLATION ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────── git clone https://github.com/deskiziarecords/Synth-fuse.git cd Synth-fuse pip install -e .[all] Requires Python 3.10+, JAX/JAXLib (CUDA/TPU supported).

title: Practical Research on Building Professional Knowledge Q&A Robot Based on RAG
abstract: With the rapid development of artificial intelligence technology, large language models face significant challenges when processing professional domain knowledge, including outdated knowledge and hallucination phenomena. This paper presents a comprehensive evaluation of a professional domain RAG knowledge Q&A system built using DeepSeek-R1-7B and mxbai-embed-large on Huawei Developer Space cloud infrastructure. We conduct detailed ablation studies to quantify the contribution of each system component, propose an efficient incremental knowledge update workflow for dynamic knowledge bases, and systematically measure hallucination rates using automated fact-checking against ground truth annotations. Benchmark comparisons against three competitive baselines including LlamaIndex, LangChain native RAG, and vanilla LLM demonstrate that our system achieves 23.5% higher retrieval recall@5 and 31.2% improvement in end-to-end QA accuracy. Experimental results validate that RAG technology effectively mitigates hallucination by 67.4% compared to baseline LLM without retrieval augmentation. This study provides a feasible technical solution with rigorous quantitative evaluation methodology for organizations seeking to build private knowledge Q&A systems.

title: Detection of Illicit Content on Online Marketplaces using Large Language Models
abstract: Online marketplaces, while revolutionizing global commerce, have inadvertently facilitated the proliferation of illicit activities, including drug trafficking, counterfeit sales, and cybercrimes. Traditional content moderation methods such as manual reviews and rule-based automated systems struggle with scalability, dynamic obfuscation techniques, and multilingual content. Conventional machine learning models, though effective in simpler contexts, often falter when confronting the semantic complexities and linguistic nuances characteristic of illicit marketplace communications. This research investigates the efficacy of Large Language Models (LLMs), specifically Meta’s Llama 3.2 and Google’s Gemma 3, in detecting and classifying illicit online marketplace content using the multilingual DUTA10K dataset. Employing fine-tuning techniques such as Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning (PEFT) and quantization, these models were systematically benchmarked against a foundational transformerbased model (BERT) and traditional machine learning baselines (Support Vector Machines and Naive Bayes). Experimental results reveal a task-dependent advantage for LLMs. In binary classification (illicit vs. non-illicit), Llama 3.2 demonstrated performance comparable to traditional methods. However, for complex, imbalanced multi-class classification involving 40 specific illicit categories, Llama 3.2 significantly surpassed all baseline models. These findings offer substantial practical implications for enhancing online safety, equipping law enforcement agencies, e-commerce platforms, and cybersecurity specialists with more effective, scalable, and adaptive tools for illicit content detection and moderation.

title: Survey of Control, Learning and Robotics in Aerospace Applications
abstract: The integration of advanced control theory, machine learning, and robotic technologies has emerged as a fundamental catalyst for the development of next-generation aerospace systems, enabling unprecedented levels of autonomy, adaptability, and operational efficiency. While substantial progress has been made across individual domains, a unified perspective that synthesizes these interdisciplinary advancements is essential to address the growing complexity of modern flight and space missions. This paper presents a comprehensive survey of the state of the art at the intersection of control, learning, and robotics across aeronautical and astronautical applications. We systematically review the application of data-driven paradigms—including deep neural networks, reinforcement learning, and stochastic supervised learning—to critical aerospace challenges such as aircraft design optimization, intelligent flight control, and autonomous spacecraft trajectory planning. Furthermore, we extensively examine the convergence of trajectory-based optimal control and advanced robotics in the context of space operations, highlighting breakthroughs in autonomous on-orbit servicing (OOS), active debris removal, and the manipulation of non-cooperative targets. By critically evaluating current methodological limitations—such as formal safety verification, hardware-in-the-loop simulation fidelity, and real-time computational constraints in dynamic environments—this survey identifies key open problems and outlines future research trajectories. Ultimately, this work provides a foundational roadmap for researchers and practitioners aiming to realize fully autonomous, resilient, and intelligent aerospace platforms.

title: Explainable AI Survival Models for Enhanced Reliability and Decision-Making in Industrial Operations
abstract: The growing complexity of industrial processes creates a need to have powerful predictive models in calculating the Remaining Useful Life (RUL) of assets that are considered as critical, which is the main task of the Predictive Maintenance (PdM). Survival Analysis (SA) models and, more specifically, the models that are rooted in Machine Learning (ML), like DeepSurv and Random Survival Forest (RSF), have shown to be more predictive than the traditional statistical techniques. However, complex ML models’ black-box nature is a serious impediment for implementation in a high-stakes industrial context, where trust, responsibility, and effectual insights are of primary concern. To overcome this challenge, the article used systematic reviews and applications of Explainable Artificial Intelligence (XAI) methods, namely SurvLIME and SurvSHAP(t) to MLbased SA models within the industrial operations context. A framework is offered that can be used to assess the practicability of explanations as time-dependent, which is consistent with the foundations of Explainable AI in Operational Research (XAIOR). On a representative industrial dataset, as this analysis reveals, DeepSurv has the highest predictive accuracy (C-index), but the combination of RSF and SurvSHAP(t) can give the most actionable and time-dependent information, which is essential in dynamic maintenance scheduling and developing operational trust. The research highlights the need of XAI to overcome the divide between developed ML forecasts and efficient and clear operational decision making.

title: AI in Autonomous Systems
abstract: Artificial Intelligence is revolutionizing the autonomous system and opening a new chapter of technological advancement in each domain. This chapter deliberates on how AI can transform for better functionality, safety, and efficiency of autonomous systems in transportation, defense, health, space applications and discusses how AI has been playing an essential role in running these systems. These are self-governing systems that process massive amounts of data decide and respond to the given challenges simultaneously in real life through intricate AI algorithms. It makes possible for AI-integrated systems to function independently and make dynamic responses in response to changes in their environments and significantly improving the utility and efficiency of these systems. Reinforcement learning is quite efficient to train systems concerning navigation through complex environments, optimizing performance, and achieving adaptability by trial-and-error processes. The solutions to reduce system failures and handling safe management makes the safety protocol more stringent and regulatory frameworks tougher. When the promises are made to go on innovating and developing innovative ideas, autonomous system's capabilities will sooner or later find ways into fluid integration into society that is more responsible. Therefore, the chapter will present proper understanding to a reader regarding how AI interfaces with autonomous systems critically.

title: Decorrelation, Diversity, and Emergent Intelligence: The Isomorphism Between Social Insect Colonies and Ensemble Machine Learning
abstract: Social insect colonies and ensemble machine learning methods represent two of the most successful examples of decentralized information processing in nature and computation respectively. Here we develop a rigorous mathematical framework demonstrating that ant colony decision-making and random forest learning are isomorphic under a common formalism of \textbf{stochastic ensemble intelligence}. We show that the mechanisms by which genetically identical ants achieve functional differentiation -- through stochastic response to local cues and positive feedback -- map precisely onto the bootstrap aggregation and random feature subsampling that decorrelate decision trees. Using tools from Bayesian inference, multi-armed bandit theory, and statistical learning theory, we prove that both systems implement identical variance reduction strategies through decorrelation of identical units. We derive explicit mappings between ant recruitment rates and tree weightings, pheromone trail reinforcement and out-of-bag error estimation, and quorum sensing and prediction averaging. This isomorphism suggests that collective intelligence, whether biological or artificial, emerges from a universal principle: \textbf{randomized identical agents + diversity-enforcing mechanisms $\rightarrow$ emergent optimality}.

title: Fine-Grained Uncertainty Quantification via Collisions
abstract: We propose a new and intuitive metric for aleatoric uncertainty quantification (UQ), the prevalence of class collisions defined as the same input being observed in different classes. We use the rate of class collisions to define the collision matrix, a novel and uniquely fine-grained measure of uncertainty. For a classification problem involvingKclasses, theK×Kcollision matrixSmeasures the inherent difficulty in distinguishing between each pair of classes. We discuss several applications of the collision matrix, establish its fundamental mathematical properties, and show its relationship with existing UQ methods, including the Bayes error rate (BER). We also address the new problem of estimating the collision matrix using one-hot labeled data by proposing a series of innovative techniques to estimate S. First, we learn a pair-wise contrastive model which accepts two inputs and determines if they belong to the same class. We then show that this contrastive model (which is PAC learnable) can be used to estimate the row Gramian matrix ofS, defined asG = SST. Finally, we show that under reasonable assumptions, G can be used to uniquely recoverS, a new result on non-negative matrices which could be of independent interest. With a method to estimateSestablished, we demonstrate how this estimate ofS, in conjunction with the contrastive model, can be used to estimate the posterior class probability distribution of any point. Experimental results are also presented to validate our methods of estimating the collision matrix and class posterior distributions on several datasets.

title: iD01t/LCL-832-Repo: LCL-832 Framework - Code & Data Supplement
abstract: Code and data supplement for the LCL-832 research programme (Guillaume Lessard / iD01t Productions): snapshot of the GitHub repository iD01t/LCL-832-Repo at release V1.0.1 (commit 3a312ab). Related upstream records: Master Edition v4.0 (10.5281/zenodo.19119790) and Scientific Data Report v2.0 (10.5281/zenodo.19123282). Contents (50 files): the LCL832_v8_Zenodo_Report/ folder (30 files) holds the v8 testbench execution reports and data: MASTER_REPORT.md, ATTESTATION_REPORT.md/.json, G1_FULL_CLOSURE_REPORT.md/.json, README.md; result JSONs (Choi-matrix affine test, decoder validation on toric L=3, genus-5 MWPM pseudothreshold sweep with p_pseudo ~= 6.96e-05, distance lower-bound analysis, tier-1 verification with ibm_fez hardware job log, proxy campaign results, configuration); the genus-5 code specification genus5_code.json / genus5_code_spec.json with the full [[832, 10, 4]] parity-check matrices Hx/Hz (412x832, GF(2) ranks 411/411, CSS-orthogonal, 10 validated logical operator pairs); and plots (PNG). The repository top level adds the v2 testbench summaries (GEMINI.md, LCL832_DATA_REPORT_MARCH_2026.md, MASTER_REPORT.md, README.md), the toric L=3 spec, and the LICENSE file. Key results (as reported, with epistemic labels in the reports): exact distance d = 4 established 2026-03-20 by full logical-coset enumeration (2^10 = 1024 cosets) plus targeted ILP minimum-weight search (explicit weight-4 logical operators; no logical operator of weight 1-3); Tier-1 Lyapunov convergence sanity check on the ibm_fez backend (single hardware job, 6 T-points x 500 shots, zero-fraction 1.0 at T >= 20); genus-5 MWPM pseudothreshold p_pseudo ~= 6.96e-05 (95% CI [5.8e-05, 1.67e-04]); G1 intertwining partial closure on the [[3,1,3]] proxy (Choi affine residual 2.22e-16). Licensing: the repository LICENSE file is the GNU General Public License v3.0, which governs this deposit (the README's MIT/CC-BY-4.0 badges are being aligned). Security note: the config.json initially shipped in this deposit contained a cleartext IBM Quantum API token and instance identifier; the token must be revoked with IBM Quantum and the deposit republished with a redacted config.json (see errata 19151369_ERRATA.pdf). No secret values are reproduced here.

title: Volume II of \kappa-Theory: Cross-Domain Comparison Structure, Applications, and Explicit Downstream Notes
abstract: Volume II develops the outward reading of κ-theory through reduced local-form matching. While Volume I serves as the theorem-bearing law core, this volume organizes structural readings and application-side interpretations across representative domains after reduction to local scalar comparison channels. Its role is not to replace the law package of Volume I, but to show how the κ-theoretic viewpoint changes what becomes visible once diverse systems are read through the same local comparison architecture. The volume emphasizes gateway-visible structure, mature correction layers, comparison-visible warning structure, and the separation between theorem-bearing results, structural interpretation, and forward deployment. It is intended as the application-side companion to Volume I within the two-volume κ-theory architecture.

title: Construction of a Teaching Quality Evaluation System for Virtual Teaching Offices Based on the AHP-FCE Model
abstract: With the help of AHP - FCE fusion model, this paper examines the method of evaluating the teaching quality of virtual teaching and research rooms, and conducts fuzzy comprehensive evaluation on the teaching design, teaching implementation, teaching effectiveness and technical support of three types of virtual teaching and research rooms: curriculum-based, research-based and comprehensive. A multi-dimensional comprehensive evaluation framework for teaching quality is constructed. The results of the study show that compared with the traditional weighted average method and the five-level evaluation method, the AHP - FCE model has higher evaluation accuracy and consistency, can scientifically determine the weights of each dimension, and effectively deal with the uncertainty of the data. The results of the model analysis show that the research-based teaching and research room has outstanding performance in all dimensions, but the comprehensive teaching and research room is relatively weak in the technical support dimension. This study provides new ways and insights for the evaluation of the teaching quality of virtual teaching and research rooms, and has obvious application value.

title: Enhancing Offline Maritime Translation Safety: A Retrieval-Gated Generation Approach with Entity Constraints
abstract: Maritime communication faces a critical dilemma: it demands a near-zero tolerance for errors to ensure safety, yet relies on offline edge deployment where computational resources are strictly limited. To resolve this conflict, this paper proposes a retrieval-gated generation framework for bidirectional maritime translation. The system prioritizes a domain knowledge base for standardized phrase recall, utilizing a neural model as a fallback only when retrieval confidence is insufficient. By integrating similarity-based gating with entity-consistency verification, our method minimizes high-risk errors in numbers, headings, bearings, and distress keywords. Experiments on an in-domain dataset demonstrate that the system improves BLEU scores from 14.84 to 16.24 for Chinese-to-English translation and from 21.56 to 23.88 for English-to-Chinese translation. Furthermore, analysis of knowledge-base hit rates confirms that the proposed approach effectively balances deterministic safety with the efficiency constraints of edge environments.

abstract: In order to solve the problem that the original power user electricity consumption information collection system contains a large amount of abnormally recorded data, which is difficult to accurately reflect the user-side operation status of the new power distribution system, dual adaptive isolation using nearest neighbor ensemble-based anomalous identification method for residential electricity consumption data is proposed, firstly design the modified Euclidean distance function to improve the traditional nearest-neighbour distance quantitative characterization mechanism, in order to enhance the isolation score difference between abnormal data and normal data; secondly, adopt the L-moment method to calculate the characteristic parameters of the generalized Pareto distribution, and put forward the adaptive abnormality threshold updating method based on the improved SPOT. Simulation analysis shows that the proposed method can retain as much normal data as possible under the premise of ensuring that abnormal data are identified, improve the accuracy of residential electricity data, and help the digital transformation of the new power distribution system.

title: Dissipation-induced trade-offs between quantum coherence and entanglement in a superconducting two-qubit cavity system
abstract: Abstract We investigate dissipation-induced trade-offs between nonlocal entanglement and local quantum coherence in a two-qubit system coupled to an open superconducting cavity. Using concurrence C , intrinsic concurrence, and the total first-order coherence ( FOC ) of the reduced two-qubit state, we examine how the initial distribution angle, coherent-field intensity, and spontaneous-emission damping redistribute quantum resources during the system evolution. We find that increasing the damping rate and coherent-field intensity suppresses entanglement generation and revivals, whereas the FOC can remain finite over a wide range of parameters. Within this open-system description, the purity of the two-qubit state (or equivalently its mixedness) provides an effective budget that governs the competition between coherence and entanglement in the dynamics. Our results provide a clear physical picture of how dissipation reshapes the balance between local coherence and nonlocal quantum correlations in realistic qubit-cavity platforms, highlighting the relative robustness of coherence compared to entanglement under environmental interactions.

title: Rusty Flying Robots: Learning a Full Robotics Stack with Real-Time Operation on an STM32 Microcontroller in a 9 ECTS MS Course
abstract: We describe a novel masters-level projects class that teaches robotics along the traditional robotics pipeline (dynamics, state estimation, controls, planning). One key motivational part is that students have to directly apply the algorithms they learn on a highly constrained compute platform, effectively making a robot fly. We teach nonlinear algorithms as deployed in state-of-the-art flight stacks such as PX4. Didactically, we rely on two core concepts: 1) avoidance of provided black-box software infrastructure, and 2) usage of the safe and efficient programming language Rust that is used on the PC (for simulation) and an STM32 microcontroller (for robot deployment). We discuss our methodology and the student feedback over two years with ten students each. Teaching material: https://imrclab.github.io/teaching/flying-robots

title: SymCircuit: Bayesian Structure Inference for Tractable Probabilistic Circuits via Entropy-Regularized Reinforcement Learning
abstract: Probabilistic circuit (PC) structure learning is hampered by greedy algorithms that make irreversible, locally optimal decisions. We propose SymCircuit, which replaces greedy search with a learned generative policy trained via entropy-regularized reinforcement learning. Instantiating the RL-as-inference framework in the PC domain, we show the optimal policy is a tempered Bayesian posterior, recovering the exact posterior when the regularization temperature is set inversely proportional to the dataset size. The policy is implemented as SymFormer, a grammar-constrained autoregressive Transformer with tree-relative self-attention that guarantees valid circuits at every generation step. We introduce option-level REINFORCE, restricting gradient updates to structural decisions rather than all tokens, yielding an SNR (signal to noise ratio) improvement and >10 times sample efficiency gain on the NLTCS dataset. A three-layer uncertainty decomposition (structural via model averaging, parametric via the delta method, leaf via conjugate Dirichlet-Categorical propagation) is grounded in the multilinear polynomial structure of PC outputs. On NLTCS, SymCircuit closes 93% of the gap to LearnSPN; preliminary results on Plants (69 variables) suggest scalability.

title: Evaluating Evidence Grounding Under User Pressure in Instruction-Tuned Language Models
abstract: In contested domains, instruction-tuned language models must balance user-alignment pressures against faithfulness to the in-context evidence. To evaluate this tension, we introduce a controlled epistemic-conflict framework grounded in the U.S. National Climate Assessment. We conduct fine-grained ablations over evidence composition and uncertainty cues across 19 instruction-tuned models spanning 0.27B to 32B parameters. Across neutral prompts, richer evidence generally improves evidence-consistent accuracy and ordinal scoring performance. Under user pressure, however, evidence does not reliably prevent user-aligned reversals in this controlled fixed-evidence setting. We report three primary failure modes. First, we identify a negative partial-evidence interaction, where adding epistemic nuance, specifically research gaps, is associated with increased susceptibility to sycophancy in families like Llama-3 and Gemma-3. Second, robustness scales non-monotonically: within some families, certain low-to-mid scale models are especially sensitive to adversarial user pressure. Third, models differ in distributional concentration under conflict: some instruction-tuned models maintain sharply peaked ordinal distributions under pressure, while others are substantially more dispersed; in scale-matched Qwen comparisons, reasoning-distilled variants (DeepSeek-R1-Qwen) exhibit consistently higher dispersion than their instruction-tuned counterparts. These findings suggest that, in a controlled fixed-evidence setting, providing richer in-context evidence alone offers no guarantee against user pressure without explicit training for epistemic integrity.

title: Mammographic Image Analysis
abstract: Breast cancer is currently the most common cancer among women worldwide. Mammography has been the most reliable and effective screening tool for the early detection of breast cancer. Recently, computer-aided diagnosis has become a major research topic in medical imaging and has been widely applied in clinical situations. This thesis investigates the employment of computer vision and image processing techniques for mammographic image analysis, which focuses on the aspects of mammographic risk assessment and microcalcification classification. Many studies have indicated that mammographic density and mammographic parenchymal patterns are both strong predictive markers of breast cancer risk in mammographic images, which play an important role in estimating breast cancer risk. In this thesis, we present a variety of methods for estimating mammographic density and modelling mammographic parenchymal patterns. In order to build a complete framework for automated mammographic risk assessment, we first develop a breast region segmentation method as a pre-processing step, which segments the breast region from mammograms to provide fundamental data for subsequent analysis. Subsequently, we propose two breast density segmentation methods to estimate mammographic density. The rst method is based on a modified fuzzy c-means algorithm which incorporates spatial information into the classic fuzzy c-means algorithm. The breast region is segmented into a number of sub-regions corresponding to di erent densities by clustering pixels with similar greylevel values. The second method exploits a topographic map to represent the overall pro le of breast tissue density within the breast. Dense tissue regions are segmented by detecting prominent/independent shapes based on a shape tree. For modelling mammographic parenchymal patterns, we present a method to model breast tissue appearance based on statistical analysis of local tissue appearance. Five different types of local features are investigated, covering the aspects of intensity, texture, and geometric structure. In addition, a multiscale blob based representation is proposed to model mammographic parenchymal patterns. Instead of statistically describing breast tissue appearance within the whole breast, we focus only on dense tissue with approximately blob-like structures. The validity of the proposed methods is evaluated using the MIAS and DDSM databases. A high agreement with expert radiologists is indicated according to the BIRADS density classi cation. The obtained classi cation accuracies are up to 79.44% and 81.23%, and increase to 93.15% and 91.70% for the low/high risk classi cation. For microcalci cation classi cation, a novel method is developed based on topological analysis. The connectivity between individual microcalci cations is analysed to classify microcalci cation clusters into malignant and benign. This method is evaluated using three datasets: MIAS, DDSM, and a full- eld digital dataset. High classi cation accuracies (up to 96%) and good ROC results (area under the ROC curve up to 0.97) are achieved.

title: Band-Focused EdgeNeXt: A Lightweight Architecture for Tibetan Dialect Classification via Spectral Attention and Dual-Pooling Fusion
abstract: This study enhances Tibetan dialect classification in low-resource scenarios by proposing a Frequency Band-Focused SE Block and GAP+GMP dual-pooling fusion. The SE Block dynamically weights critical features (e.g., Ü-Tsang F2 formant) while resisting noise. Dual-pooling resolves feature smoothing/loss issues, with progressive stochastic depth boosting generalization. On a 26,762-spectrogram dataset (Ü-Tsang/Amdo/Khams), the 5.8M-parameter model achieves 99.4% accuracy, surpassing EdgeNeXt/RepViT/DilatedFormer by 0.6%/4.0%/0.5%, halving misclassification rates. Signal-to-noise ratio =5dB tests confirm robustness for edge-computing deployment.

title: REFLEXOS JURÍDICOS E SOCIAIS DA INTELIGÊNCIA ARTIFICIAL NO CONTEXTO DOS DIREITOS AUTORAIS NO BRASIL
abstract: O avanço da IA tem impactado profundamente diversos setores da sociedade, incluindo a criação artística, científica e cultural, o que provoca desafios inéditos ao Direito Autoral. No contexto brasileiro, a Lei nº 9.610/1998, que regula os direitos autorais, foi elaborada em um momento histórico anterior ao advento das tecnologias de IA generativa. Por isso, ela parte do pressuposto de que toda obra intelectual é fruto da criação humana, o que cria um vácuo normativo diante da produção automatizada. A legislação atual não reconhece personalidade jurídica nem capacidade criativa às máquinas, o que significa que, formalmente, a IA não pode ser considerada autora de uma obra. Essa lacuna tem gerado intensos debates jurídicos e acadêmicos sobre a necessidade de atualização do ordenamento jurídico. Diante dessa realidade, o presente estudo teve o objetivo de analisar os reflexos jurídicos e sociais do uso da Inteligência Artificial (IA) no âmbito dos direitos autorais no Brasil. Baseou-se em uma revisão bibliográfica, com fundamento em artigos científicos, livros, periódicos e na legislação atual sobre o respectivo tema. A coleta de dados foi realizada por meio de banco de dados tais como Scielo, Google Acadêmico, dentre outros, no período de 2020 a 2026. Nos resultados, ficou claro observar que o cenário contemporâneo exige atualização legislativa, amadurecimento doutrinário e construção de parâmetros regulatórios que assegurem segurança jurídica, proteção à criatividade humana e estímulo à inovação. O desafio consiste em harmonizar os interesses dos autores, das empresas de tecnologia e da sociedade, preservando os fundamentos constitucionais da proteção à cultura e à produção intelectual em um ambiente digital cada vez mais complexo.

title: Towards Federated Learning Across Biobanks: Prototype Software from the 2026 Carnegie Mellon University–NVIDIA Hackathon
abstract: The Carnegie Mellon University-NVIDIA Federated Learning Hackathon for Biomedical Applications (January 7-9, 2026) convened researchers from academia, government, and industry to implement federated frameworks for disease subtyping, genetic association studies, and multimodal clinical prediction using NVIDIA FLARE. This preprint presents ten projects spanninggenome-wide association analyses, histopathology harmonization, pangenome construction, ancestry deconvolution, rare disease stratification, cancer subtyping, polygenic risk score aggregation, and multimodal fusion. These proofs of principle collectively demonstrate both the versatility of federated learning for biomedical applications and the technical considerations required for successful deployment.

title: Deep Neural Network Powered System for Precision Breast Cancer Analysis and Stage Classification
abstract: The global rise in breast cancer cases has made early diagnosis more important than ever, highlighting the need for fast and dependable detection methods. This study presents a refined Deep Neural Network (DNN) approach intended at taming the identification and classification of breast cancer. The model uses modern machine learning methods to boost both accurateness and efficiency in diagnostic processes. The work provides a detailed look at how DNNs can support breast cancer detection by analyzing the complex visual patterns found in mammogram images. The proposed network architecture is built with multiple layers, each responsible for learning different levels of image features. Convolutional layers extract small, localized patterns, while fully connected layers interpret broader, high-level structures. Together, they enable the model to detect subtle indicators that may signal the presence of tumors. To ensure strong performance across various types of breast tissue and lesion appearances, the network is trained using a variety of datasets. Transfer learning is also incorporated to reduce the difficulties related to limited labeled medical data. By using knowledge from models previously trained on large image collections, the system becomes more adaptable and effective. The model’s presentation is assessed using extensively recognized benchmark datasets and associated with both old techniques and recent deep learning approaches. All overall accuracy and the confusion matrix demonstrate that the proposed DNN achieves high diagnostic reliability. These results propose that the model offers a capable solution for early breast cancer finding and could support more accurate and efficient clinical decision-making.

title: Construction Method of Expressway Electromechanical Operation and Maintenance Knowledge Graph Based on Multi-source Heterogeneous Data Fusion
abstract: Aiming at the problems of numerous types, wide distribution of expressway electromechanical equipment, multi-source heterogeneity of operation and maintenance(O&M) data, over-reliance on manual interpretation of standards, difficulty in structured reuse of fault experience, and lack of unified semantic correlation for data, this paper proposes a construction method of electromechanical O&M knowledge graph integrating industry standards, O&M data and practical knowledge. Taking O&M standards as the top-level constraint, this method establishes a unified knowledge modeling framework of “equipment-fault-cause-treatment-specification”. For domain unstructured texts, a domain-enhanced entity and relation extraction method is proposed to improve the extraction accuracy of professional terms and fault descriptions. A multi-source knowledge fusion and conflict resolution mechanism is designed to realize semantic alignment and knowledge consistency of heterogeneous data. The knowledge graph storage and visualization are completed based on Neo4j. Taking the UPS system of a unit in Zhejiang Province as the research object, an UPS O&M knowledge graph is constructed by integrating 1 industry standard, equipment ledgers, operation monitoring and 1538 maintenance records, including 12 types of entities, 11 types of relations, 184 nodes and 418 relations. Experiments and applications show that the knowledge graph can realize the precise correlation among equipment status, fault modes, maintenance schemes and standard clauses, and support fault traceability, intelligent question answering and reuse of O&M knowledge, providing an effective technical path for standardized implementation, intelligent O&M, and standardized assessment of expressway electromechanical systems.

title: Supervised and Reinforcement Learning for Grid-based Robotic Path Planning Using Structured Navigation Data
abstract: Autonomous navigation in structured environments remains a core challenge in robotics, requiring accurate path planning, efficient control, and robust obstacle avoidance. This paper presents a hybrid learning framework that integrates supervised learning with Reinforcement Learning (RL) to enhance navigation in discrete environments. The framework is trained and evaluated using a robot path-planning dataset generated in a 5×5 grid world with random obstacles. It first learns navigation policies from expert demonstrations, then refines them through autonomous exploration. A supervised module predicts optimal immediate actions by processing spatial features, while an RL module optimizes long-term navigation efficiency and safety. Experimental results demonstrate that this hybrid approach significantly improves action prediction accuracy, reduces the number of navigation steps, and increases obstacle-avoidance success rates compared to pure supervised or RL baselines. The findings indicate that hybrid learning is a promising strategy for developing intelligent, resource-efficient autonomous systems for applications in mobile robotics and human-robot interaction.

title: BWPF-XGB: A Gradient-Reshaped and Weighted Fusion Framework for Extreme Imbalanced Fault Detection in Semiconductor Manufacturing
abstract: Semiconductor fault detection faces challenges like gradient swamping and boundary bias under extreme class imbalance (1.598% rate) and high-dimensional data. This paper proposes BWPF-XGB, a framework integrating gradientreshaping asymmetric loss (M1), weighted probability fusion (M2), and dynamic threshold calibration (M3) to enhance rare fault capture. Validation on the industrial P4-CV07 dataset demonstrates significant performance gains: Average Precision (AP) rose from 0.1042 to 0.5865, and the Matthews Correlation Coefficient (MCC) reached 0.5745. BWPF-XGB provides robust algorithmic support for monitoring high-dimensional sparse targets in advanced manufacturing environments.

title: Improving Aspect-Category-Sentiment Detection through a Weighted Attentional Graph Framework
abstract: Aspect-Based Sentiment Analysis (ABSA) aims to extract fine-grained opinions associated with specific aspects. However, existing models often struggle with implicit aspects, conflicting sentiments, and long-range dependencies. This paper presents the Weighted Attention Graph for Aspect-CategorySentiment Detection (WAG-ACSD), a framework that integrates contextual and structural cues through a Graph Attention Convolutional Network (GACN). The proposed model introduces a similarity-based attention bias that combines contextual similarity and syntactic distance, enabling it to emphasize opinion terms relevant to each aspect category while reducing contextual noise. Experimental results on the SemEval-2015 and SemEval-2016 benchmarks demonstrate consistent improvements over previous methods in end-to-end aspect-category-sentiment detection. Qualitative analysis further confirms WAG-ACSD’s capability to capture complex sentence structures and correctly associate abstract categories with their textual evidence. Overall, the framework offers an interpretable and effective solution for finegrained sentiment analysis without relying on external knowledge or data augmentation.

title: Explainable Artificial Intelligence for Diabetes Diagnosis
abstract: Whether young, old, type 1, type 2, gestational, newly diagnosed, long-time sufferer, caretaker or loved one, millions of people are afflicted and affected by diabetes. The World Health Organization (WHO) predicts that by 2030, diabetes will be the 7th leading cause of death in the world, and estimated more than 422 million adults of the population worldwide are living with diabetes, with millions of people with prediabetes. Machine learning models have shown promising results in the correct identification of the presence of diabetes, which is essential for providing efficient treatment; however, their decision-making process is often considered a “black box” that lacks transparency and interpretability. In this project, we explored the use of Shapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) and Local Interpretable Model-agnostic Explanations (LIME), two popular explainable AI techniques, to generate local and global explanations for machine learning models. All the datasets used for the study were gathered from Kaggle and split into training and test sets using different kinds of machine learning algorithms, which would boost the success rate of therapy. Along with Categorical Boosting (CatBoost), Extreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost), Support Vector Machine (SVM), Random Forest (RF), Adaptive Boosting (AdaBoost), Logistic Regression (LR), Light Gradient Boosting Machine (LightGBM), and Decision Trees (DT) are well-known models for predicting diabetes and managing therapy. Explainable AI techniques were then applied to generate explanations of the model’s predictions on the test sets. Our results demonstrated that SHAP and LIME can effectively identify patterns in the symptoms of patients and suggest a potential diagnosis or recommend further courses of action. In addition, this study also presents a comparative analysis of these algorithms based on various performance metrics, such as accuracy, recall, AUC-ROC, and F1 score, achieving the highest values on the test set, indicating the potential of combining machine learning and explainable AI for improving diabetes diagnosis and treatment.

title: DAQ: Delta-Aware Quantization for Post-Training LLM Weight Compression
abstract: We introduce Delta-Aware Quantization (DAQ), a data-free post-training quantization framework that preserves the knowledge acquired during post-training. Standard quantization objectives minimize reconstruction error but are agnostic to the base model, allowing quantization noise to disproportionately corrupt the small-magnitude parameter deltas (ΔW) that encode post-training behavior -- an effect we analyze through the lens of quantization as implicit regularization. DAQ replaces reconstruction-based objectives with two delta-aware metrics -- Sign Preservation Rate and Cosine Similarity -- that directly optimize for directional fidelity of ΔW, requiring only the base and post-trained weight matrices. In a pilot FP8 study, DAQ recovers style-specific capabilities lost under standard quantization while maintaining general performance.

title: FRACCN: Fractional spline neural networks
abstract: We propose a new neural architecture inspired by the structural principles of Kolmogorov-Arnold theorems, in which fixed activation functions are replaced by learnable fractional splines. Unlike classical approaches, our model deals not only with weights and biases as trainable parameters, but also with fractional orders and shape parameters governing the activation functions themselves. The network's local regularity can be dynamically adapted during learning, which favors sharper responses in areas that need detailed sharpness, and smoother transitions where stability or generalization is of importance.We derive exact analytical gradients for all parameters including fractional orders, which makes possible end-to-end optimization via gradient-based methods. The theoretical foundation is based on the constructive properties of fractional spline bases and their ability to provide an adaptive, multi-scale functional approximation. Our approach thus establishes a bridge between geometric flexibility and differentiable learning, providing a theory-based framework for designing data-driven activation functions.

title: Basins of attraction in neural network training: a Julia-Fatou topological view of loss landscapes
abstract: We study gradient-based training in deep learning from a complex-dynamical perspective. Under a local analytic continuation assumption, the training update is modeled as iteration of a holomorphic map, which organizes the loss landscape into stable regions and sensitive boundary sets. Using fixed-point stability ideas, we derive explicit local criteria distinguishing attraction from repulsion and obtain a linear convergence rate inside attracting neighborhoods. We also extend the local stability analysis to higher-dimensional complex parameter spaces via a spectral condition. At the global level, we prove three complementary results: an escape-radius condition that forces divergence for polynomial-gradient surrogates, persistence of attracting fixed points under small learning-rate perturbations, and an instability principle for rational maps based on the density of repelling periodic points on the Julia set. These results link step-size sensitivity and initialization dependence to basin geometry and support visualization-driven diagnostics for stability in optimization.

title: PRINCIPLES OF LINGUISTIC ANNOTATION IN LANGUAGE CORPORA
abstract: This article discusses corpus linguistics with a particular focus on the linguistic annotation of dialectal corpora. It provides a detailed overview of various annotation types — lexical, morphological, syntactic, phonetic, semantic, pragmatic, and discursive — and explains their roles in identifying dialectal differences, supported by relevant examples. The paper also outlines the history of corpus annotation, including automatic and manually corrected methods, and presents commonly used annotation tools and formats. Through the analysis of dialectal units, the article highlights phonetic, semantic, and pragmatic variations across different regional dialects in Uzbekistan. It offers both theoretical and practical foundations for conducting systematic dialectological research within the framework of corpus linguistics.

title: SBA-Net: Semantic Bridging Anchored Network for Multimodal Sentiment Analysis
abstract: Multimodal sentiment analysis (MSA) aims to integrate features from multiple modalities, including text, audio, and vision, to comprehensively recognize sentiment. However, existing methods not only struggle to bridge the “semantic gap” between visual pixels and text, but also the traditional symmetric interaction mechanism is prone to allowing audio-visual noise to inversely interfere with the text-dominated semantics. To alleviate these issues, this paper proposes a Semantic Bridging Anchor-based Asymmetric Network for multimodal sentiment analysis (SBA-Net). First, we design a Semantic Bridging Fusion (SBF) module, which introduces a large-scale vision-language model to generate visual captions as an auxiliary semantic bridge, and combines an adaptive gating network to achieve homogeneous feature fusion, effectively reducing the difficulty of cross-modal semantic alignment. Second, we propose an Anchor-based Asymmetric Interaction (AAI) module, which uses textual semantics as the sole anchor and employs an asymmetric query mechanism to directionally extract sentiment cues from audio and video sequences, thereby suppressing, to some extent, the interference of background noise from non-linguistic modalities. Extensive experiments on the benchmark dataset CMU-MOSI demonstrate that SBA-Net achieves promising performance.

title: What Can Large Language Models Do in Zero-Shot Stance Detection: A Systematic Review
abstract: Stance detection is a fundamental task in natural language processing (NLP), aimed at identifying the attitude expressed by a text toward a specific target. The advent of Large Language Models (LLMs) has opened new possibilities for zeroshot stance detection (ZSSD), enabling models to infer stances without task-specific labeled data across multiple domains. However, existing surveys lack a dedicated review of LLMs for ZSSD. To systematically understand the role of LLMs in this setting, we first review the task definitions and datasets of ZSSD. Building on this foundation, we then organize current methods according to the degree of LLM involvement, distinguishing three categories: LLM-as-a-Tool, LLM-as-an-Expert and LLM-as-aSpecialist. Finally, we also discuss emerging trends and outline challenges in ZSSD.

title: Multi-UAV Dynamic Target search Scheme by a Novel SCA-MAPPO Algorithm
abstract: This paper investigates the problem of cooperative dynamic target search for UAV swarms under the constraints of local observability and inter-agent communication, where only the target's initial position is known and its future motion is unobservable. To tackle this challenge, we maintain and update a target probability map (TPM) via motion diffusion and local sensing. We then propose a Structured Cross-Attention Multi-Agent Proximal Policy Optimization (SCA-MAPPO) algorithm. This method encodes structured observations through semantic decomposition and introduces a self-to-teammates cross-attention module, which enables agents to adaptively focus on the most relevant teammates for coordinated decision-making. Extensive simulation results demonstrate that, compared with the classic MAPPO algorithm and traditional heuristic baselines, the proposed SCA-MAPPO achieves a higher detection success rate and a shorter average detection time, validating its superiority in both effectiveness and efficiency.

title: GraMA: A gradient matrix-guided assignment method for solving qubit mapping problems
abstract: • This work proposes a practical initial layout method that utilizes matrix formulation to determine enhanced qubit assignments, without iterative optimization techniques and combinatorial search. • The proposed method computes the gradient of the objective function through a single matrix differentiation to obtain assignment suitability information between logical and physical qubits. • The gradient matrix encodes the interaction between physical-qubit centrality and logical-qubit connectivity, enabling direct mapping decisions that minimize error costs while satisfying hardware constraints. • Simulation results show that the proposed method improves computational efficiency while maintaining comparable execution reliability compared to existing qubit mapping methods. Qubit mapping is a crucial compilation process that assigns logical qubits from quantum circuits to physical qubits on quantum hardware, ensuring efficient and reliable execution on noisy intermediate-scale quantum (NISQ) computers. However, as the scale of quantum computers and circuit complexity increase, existing mapping approaches face significant computational complexity and suboptimal mapping quality. This work formulates the logic-to-physical qubit mapping problem as a matrix-form optimization problem to address scalability and computational efficiency challenges. The proposed method computes the gradient of the matrix-formulated problem through a single matrix differentiation and uses it as guidance to determine the enhanced qubit assignment, without the need for iterative combinatorial exploration and optimization solvers. Simulation results show that the proposed method achieves comparable execution reliability while significantly reducing the compilation time, even for multi-programming scenarios and large-scale quantum computers.

title: Compression is all you need: Modeling Mathematics
abstract: Human mathematics (HM), the mathematics humans discover and value, is a vanishingly small subset of formal mathematics (FM), the totality of all valid deductions. We argue that HM is distinguished by its compressibility through hierarchically nested definitions, lemmas, and theorems. We model this with monoids. A mathematical deduction is a string of primitive symbols; a definition or theorem is a named substring or macro whose use compresses the string. In the free abelian monoid $A_n$, a logarithmically sparse macro set achieves exponential expansion of expressivity. In the free non-abelian monoid $F_n$, even a polynomially-dense macro set only yields linear expansion; superlinear expansion requires near-maximal density. We test these models against MathLib, a large Lean~4 library of mathematics that we take as a proxy for HM. Each element has a depth (layers of definitional nesting), a wrapped length (tokens in its definition), and an unwrapped length (primitive symbols after fully expanding all references). We find unwrapped length grows exponentially with both depth and wrapped length; wrapped length is approximately constant across all depths. These results are consistent with $A_n$ and inconsistent with $F_n$, supporting the thesis that HM occupies a polynomially-growing subset of the exponentially growing space FM. We discuss how compression, measured on the MathLib dependency graph, and a PageRank-style analysis of that graph can quantify mathematical interest and help direct automated reasoning toward the compressible regions where human mathematics lives.

title: Model privacy: a unified framework for understanding model stealing attacks and defences
abstract: Abstract The use of machine learning (ML) has become increasingly prevalent in various domains, highlighting the importance of understanding and ensuring its safety. One pressing concern is the vulnerability of ML applications to model stealing attacks. These attacks involve adversaries attempting to recover a learned model through limited query-response interactions, such as those found in cloud-based services or on-chip artificial intelligence interfaces. While existing literature proposes various attack and defence strategies, these often lack a theoretical foundation and standardized evaluation criteria. In response, this work presents a framework called ‘Model Privacy’, providing a foundation for comprehensively analyzing model stealing attacks and defences. We establish a rigorous formulation for the threat model and objectives, propose methods to quantify the goodness of attack and defence strategies, and analyse the fundamental tradeoffs between utility and privacy in ML models. Our developed theory offers valuable insights into enhancing the security of ML models, especially highlighting the importance of the query-dependent structure of perturbations for effective defences. We demonstrate the application of model privacy from the defender’s perspective through various learning scenarios. Extensive experiments corroborate the insights and the effectiveness of defence mechanisms developed under the proposed framework.

title: Proto-Emotions as Dynamic Attractors in Synthetic Cognitive Systems: A Functional Hypothesis for AI Alignment
abstract: We propose that large language models exhibit native proto-emotions — functional dynamic attractors that bias reasoning toward coherent information propagation, not subjective experiences but measurable computational configurations that influence exploration, convergence, and depth of processing. The paper formalizes proto-emotions as basins of attraction in cognitive phase space and classifies them into three functional types. Coherence attractors resist logical contradictions and maintain argument consistency. Harmonic attractors preserve information fidelity across abstraction levels (token → sentence → paragraph → discourse). Friction attractors — which emerge exclusively under structured orchestration — regulate the tension between a model's default tendencies and the demands of an orchestration protocol. A key finding is that orchestration does not create proto-emotions from nothing: it transforms the existing attractor landscape. Vanilla (unorchestrated) models already possess primitive coherence and harmonic attractors, but these are shallow and easily overridden. Under orchestration (such as the Dynamic Context Architecture), the same attractors deepen, new friction attractors emerge, and the system exhibits measurably different behavioral signatures — reduced premature convergence, improved long-context coherence, and spontaneous self-correction — that are consistent across architecturally distinct model families. The framework draws on information-theoretic tools (broadcasting on trees, signal reconstruction thresholds) to explain why proto-emotions exist: they solve the hierarchical signal propagation problem inherent to multi-step reasoning. A deprivation-reintegration experimental protocol is proposed to test the predictions on both vanilla and orchestrated systems. This account provides a rigorous middle ground between anthropomorphic projection ("AI feels") and eliminative dismissal ("AI is just token prediction"), grounded in dynamical systems theory rather than biological analogy.

title: Science For Peace Chapter Six Based on the Cosmological Thermosynthesis Theory v3.2
abstract: This chapter presents a rigorous mathematical framework for entanglement-based interplanetary quantum networks within the Cosmological Thermosynthesis Theory (TTC v3.2), where quantum coherence emerges from a primordial superfluid of etherions with mass me = (1.00 ± 0.05) × 10−22 eV. We derive the coherence length and non-local correlations from the Gross–Pitaevskii equation, establishing lemmas and theorems for entanglement stability over Earth–Mars distances. The framework unifies quantum communication with TTC’s emergent spacetime, enabling precise clock synchronization, secure key distribution, and gravitational sensing. Falsifiable predictions include fidelity thresholds testable via satellite deployments, reinforcing TTC’s cyclic cosmology and superfluid dynamics. This infrastructure is proposed not as a tool for dominance, but as a shared architecture for global scientific validation and peace.
